summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for evaluation of lower abdominal discomfort and to complete a colonoscopy, which required PICC line placement due to difficult IV access. She had chronic lower extremity edema and a history of recurrent cellulitis, currently improving on clindamycin. Abdominal pain was localized to the left lower pannus, and imaging ruled out abscess or obstruction, supporting a diagnosis of panniculitis. A colonoscopy revealed and removed polyps in the ascending and sigmoid colon, with internal hemorrhoids noted. She was subtherapeutic on warfarin on admission, requiring bridging with heparin until INR reached 2.0. Despite recommendations, she refused her diuretic for the final two days of admission, resulting in increased peripheral edema, but remained asymptomatic with clear lungs. She was discharged home against medical advice regarding diuresis, with instructions to resume torsemide and follow up on polyp biopsies and anticoagulation management.
